balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

interestIncomeMix.title: Gross vs net interest income
interestIncomeMix.content:
Gross interest income is the total interest earned on loans and securities before deducting what the bank pays out on deposits and wholesale funding; net interest income (NII) is what's left after that interest expense.

For Shinhan Financial Group: the spread between the two lines is interest expense -- it tracks funding cost, which moves with Bank of Korea policy rates and competition for deposits, not with loan growth.

What to watch:

  • Gross interest income rising while NII is flat or falling -- funding costs eating the spread
  • The gap widening faster than the loan book grows

feeIncome.title: Fee & commission income vs net interest income
feeIncome.content:
Net fee & commission income is revenue from banking, card, trust, brokerage and wealth-management services -- earned without taking on interest-rate or credit risk, unlike NII.

For Shinhan Financial Group: a group with card, securities and asset-management subsidiaries alongside the bank, fee income is the diversification signal -- it should move independently of the interest-rate cycle that drives NII.

What to watch:

  • Fee income shrinking as a share of total income (more reliant on the rate cycle)
  • Fee income growth outpacing NII growth in a falling-rate environment

hybridBonds.title: AT1 hybrid bonds vs common equity
hybridBonds.content:
AT1 hybrid bonds (perpetual, contingently-convertible instruments) count as regulatory and accounting equity but are not common equity -- they carry a coupon, rank ahead of common shareholders, and dilute nothing unless triggered.

For Shinhan Financial Group: hybrid bonds have grown faster than common equity over the last decade, so reported shareholders' equity increasingly overstates the common-equity cushion -- the DCF and any book-value multiple should use TotalCommonEquity, not ShareholdersEquity.

What to watch:

  • Hybrid bonds growing faster than common equity (rising reliance on AT1 issuance for capital ratios)
  • Coupon cost on hybrids versus the return they let the bank hold onto by satisfying Basel requirements

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Shinhan Financial Group Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
